features.name: any_oc_comment_has_decimal
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain a decimal number such as 3.14 or 0.75?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments with json.loads into a list of strings. Return 1 if any comment matches regex r'(?<![\w.])\d+\.\d+(?![\w]*\.\d)' (digits, a period, digits; e.g. 3.14, 0.75, 2.5, 1.96), else 0. Empty list gives 0. Missing or unparseable OC_comments gives null. Raw text match, no semantic filtering; version numbers or IP-like strings may match, and sentence-ending periods without digits after do not.

h0: any_oc_comment_has_decimal has no association with the probability that the OP changed their view.
h1: Discussions with any_oc_comment_has_decimal = 1 have a higher rate of OP view change than those with 0.
note: Persuasiveness is operationalized as the supplied delta outcome (OP view change) at row level. Comments are unordered and have no per-comment outcomes, so the test is whether a discussion has at least one decimal-containing counter-comment. This is an association, not causal. The raw text could include outcome announcements or later replies, and its timing is unknown. The regex is mechanical: it may match non-quantitative decimals such as version numbers, and it does not separate quoted text from the commenter's own words.
